clue.text: To do catechism "freestyle" is about right for this teaching

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are said to be about, that is to surround, the next piece
in quotes, freestyle means done without set form, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged at will

explanation.surface: A teacher plans to run a catechism class in a loose, improvised way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freestyle' shuffles TO DO CATECHISM, and 'is about' wraps that mix round R for right. 'for' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher's method teaches by a chain of probing questions and answers, much like a catechism.

clue.text: Hackney united to split old lines

indicators.note: the united piece is put in to split the other pieces apart, so it goes inside them

parts.note: lines of poetry make up verse
U is the standard abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A London borough's sports club joins forces to break up some ancient boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a London borough in the surface, but here it is the verb 'to hackney', to make trite through repeated use. 'to split' puts U inside O + VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hackney a phrase is to wear it out by repeating it until it becomes stale.

clue.text: Government erected section of Tangiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, something erected is built upwards, so the letters are read from bottom to top
only a section of the place name gives the letters needed, a run inside the word

explanation.surface: An administration has put up a part of the Moroccan port city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section of' takes NGIER from inside Tangiers, and 'erected' reads it upwards, giving the five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of rule is their government of the country.

clue.text: NYC tower owner deceived one, raising the lowest without foundation

parts.note: Donald Trump owns Trump Tower in New York City

indicators.note: in a down clue the lowest letter of the word is the last one, and it is lifted up to the top

parts.note: a dupe is a person who has been deceived

explanation.surface: The New York skyscraper's proprietor fooled someone while raising the poorest without any basis.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the 'lowest' letter is the last, so 'raising the lowest' moves the final E of the dupe to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumped-up charges are fabricated ones with no basis in fact.

clue.text: Care about changing route, frequency and hours somewhat? I don't

indicators.note: about means in a different arrangement here, so the four letters before it are rearranged
the route is changing, so its letters are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: somewhat means a little, a bit

explanation.surface: A commuter is told to vary their route, timetable and hours a little, and protests that they never do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'changing' are two separate anagram signals, one per word. The definition is the speaker's reply 'I don't' (change), which describes someone stuck in routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses to alter their routine is a person ruled by fixed custom.

clue.text: Tree having lived longer

definitions.meaning: a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a berry-bearing tree and the person of greater age.

clue.text: Read Smith's stirring novel

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the two words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter, leaving the name as written

explanation.surface: A recommendation to read an exciting book by an author named Smith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like praise for the novel but shuffles READ SMITH. The answer is the Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens wrote a novel of this title set in an industrial northern town.

clue.text: Rep rashly taking turns with fool in a bit of a fog?

indicators.note: something done rashly is done without care, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: a dolt is a fool

explanation.surface: A sales rep hastily takes turns with an idiot in the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking turns with' describes the result: the shuffled letters of REP alternate with the letters of DOLT, D-R-O-P-L-E-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Fog is made of countless tiny suspended drops of water, so one drop is a small part of it.

clue.text: Common conclusion on past form: one caught in innocent grooming

indicators.note: the three pieces are placed in the word for innocent

parts.note: innocent means pure
the common ending of an English past-tense verb form is -ed
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone innocent, but with a past record, is caught out while being groomed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'past form' is a verb in the past tense, whose usual ending is -ed; 'grooming' here is care of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatment of the feet and toenails is a form of personal care.

clue.text: Irish man kicked back, circling room

indicators.note: the reversed word circles, or surrounds, the abbreviation for room
back means the word for kicked is read from right to left

parts.note: to toe something is to kick it

explanation.surface: An Irishman lashed out and went round the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word for kicked round to DEOT before 'circling' wraps it round the room.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional Irish boy's name, as in Dermot Morgan.

clue.text: How to derive an irrational root

indicators.note: the answer read as an instruction says how to get a number: these words point to that instruction

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number, and turning the letters I and P round gives it

explanation.surface: A mathematical instruction for extracting an irrational square root.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about square roots. Split the answer after four letters and it reads as an instruction to turn IP round, which gives PI, an irrational number; the whole is a root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded white vegetable grown for its swollen edible root.

clue.text: Motor control is hard in gait let loose

indicators.note: the letter for hard is placed in the word for the gait

parts.note: a trot is a horse's gait
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: let loose means the letters of let are set free to take a new order

explanation.surface: Controlling one's movement is difficult when one's walk has run free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gait' is not anagram fodder: it gives a synonym, and only 'let' is let loose, becoming TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve or pedal that regulates fuel reaching an engine controls its speed.

clue.text: Ultimately, Bosie and his lover entering had children in perplexity

indicators.note: the pieces are entering, going inside, the word for had children

parts.note: bred means produced offspring

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the name that follows

parts.note: Bosie, Lord Alfred Douglas, was the lover of Oscar Wilde

explanation.surface: In the end Bosie and his lover came into a family, to general confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bosie was the nickname of Lord Alfred Douglas, Oscar Wilde's lover; 'Ultimately' takes the last letter of Bosie.
explanation.definitionFit: Being utterly puzzled and confused is to be in a state of perplexity.

clue.text: Doctors swallowing ecstasy, doctors coming up on it, suited convention?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for doctors swallows, or holds inside, the drug's letter

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: docs is informal for doctors
it refers back to the ecstasy just named, giving another E

explanation.surface: Doctors high on ecstasy turn up for a formal-wear event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the second doctors round to SCOD; 'it' then refers back to ecstasy for the final E. The question mark flags 'suited' as wearing a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule on what clothes must be worn, such as jacket and tie, is a convention about being suited.

clue.text: Dog meat? That's not on!

indicators.note: not on means the two letters on are left out of the meat

parts.note: mutton is the meat of sheep
the two letters of the word are what is removed

explanation.surface: A diner objects that the dish is dog meat, which is not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on!' reads as an objection, but 'not' removes ON from MUTTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel of mixed breed is called a mutt.

clue.text: Combs over after odd cutting: it's not out of place in winds

definitions.text: it's not out of place in winds

indicators.note: after the odd-numbered letters are cut away, the even ones remain

explanation.surface: Combing over one's hair after a strange haircut doesn't look odd on a windy day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after odd cutting' removes the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of COMBS OVER, leaving O, B, O, E. 'winds' is the woodwind section, not weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument belongs in an orchestra's wind section.

to make a smart, striking impression

parts.note: a pedal is part of a piano

explanation.surface: A request to press the soft or loud control on a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push' looks like the action on the pedal but is the definition, to sell or promote hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To push goods or ideas is to hawk them, selling persistently.

clue.text: Place to pick up volume acceptable in rubbish work

indicators.note: the word for acceptable goes in the word for rubbish

explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' is a book, not loudness, and the acceptable letters sit inside the rubbish after its first two letters.

clue.text: Start working dry hotel, keeping male support slight?

parts.note: to kick in is to start operating

indicators.note: the dry abbreviation keeps the other pieces inside it

a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.walkthrough: 'support' is a golf tee, and the question mark marks 'slight' as a figurative snub rather than meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp rebuff or humiliating setback is felt as a slight.
